newsitem.title: UK: UK assay office increase hallmarking in 1st quarter.
newsitem.headline: UK assay office increase hallmarking in 1st quarter.

text.p: The number of gold items hallmarked at the four UK assay offices in the first quarter of 1997 rose by 8.7 percent from the same period in 1996 to 3,316,808, a statement said on Thursday.
Of the total 2,212,745 were manufactured in Britain and 1,104,063 were of foreign origin.

The nine carat items continued to to dominate the gold statistics with a total of 2,794,297 but the biggest percentage rise came in the 22 carat gold items which showed a 53.6 percent increase to 222,059 hallmarked pieces.
Of the total for 22-carat gold, foreign fabricated items rose 60 percent to 111,242 and the number of domestically fabricated items increased 47.7 percent to 110,817.
By weight, the total gold hallmark rose 14.1 percent to 14,990,465 grams.
The 1,339,175 silver items hallmarked showed a rise of 23.4 percent. The number of foreign items increased 51.6 percent to 447,392 while the domestic items rose 12.9 percent to 891,783.
Platinum items hallmarked showed an increase of 56.2 percent to 10,151 with foreign fabricated items rising 77.9 percent to 434 and UK-manufactured items increasing 55.4 percent to 9,717.

By weight, silver items hallmarked was a rise of 19.3 percent to 29,518 grams while the 70,152 grams of platinum items passing through the assay offices represented an increase of 71.2 percent from the same period in 1996.
